topics.topic: Whether open_store and startup recovery may create, inspect, modify, or remove artifact and spool storage despite the exclusivity claim
questions: Must open_store remain allowed to create and clean the content-addressed and spool areas, or must the claim that those areas are read and written only by publishing functions be narrowed?

Must open_store remain allowed to read and modify the content-addressed area and run spool during recovery, or must the record_change note limit its exclusivity claim to normal publication functions while expressly excluding startup recovery?
Must the exclusivity claim be narrowed to record_change itself, or must open_store stop creating, inspecting and removing content-area and spool artifacts?
Must the exclusivity claim allow open_store and run recovery to remove artifacts, or must the stated start-up cleanup behavior change?

quotes: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST NOT publish, rewrite or re-check value bytes or a spooled file: a StoredValue carries no bytes, and record_change writes only records, so the content-addressed area and the run spool are read and written only by the functions that publish them.

open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on data_directory itself, opened as a directory without following links and held for the life of the process, so the lock creates no file; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the temporary files an interrupted publish left in the content-addressed area and every file of that area whose digest no StoredValue names — a trial case's file fixture is itself a StoredValue of file carriage (M21), so no other record names a value file —, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area when absent; last, call remove_spool_temporaries for data_directory, which creates the spool area when absent and removes the temporaries of an interrupted spool publish, re-raising its SpoolInternalError as StoreInternalError.
judgement.why: open_store is required to inspect, create, and remove content-area and spool artifacts even though the new exclusivity clause permits those areas to be read and written only by publishing functions.

topics.topic: Whether read_value_bytes may read both artifact storage areas despite the exclusivity claim
questions: Must read_value_bytes remain allowed to read both artifact areas, or must the claim that only publishing functions read them be changed?
Must read_value_bytes remain allowed to read both storage areas, or must the record_change note say that only the designated publication, reading, and recovery functions may access them?
Must the exclusivity claim permit read_value_bytes to read both artifact areas, or must read_value_bytes no longer perform the required reads?

quotes: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST NOT publish, rewrite or re-check value bytes or a spooled file: a StoredValue carries no bytes, and record_change writes only records, so the content-addressed area and the run spool are read and written only by the functions that publish them.

read_value_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] For a stored_value source MUST look up the StoredValue by value_id with load_stored_value_row and read the bytes of its value_digest from the content-addressed area (for a value carriage these are its canonical JSON bytes); for a spooled_file source MUST look up the SpooledFile by its full key with load_spooled_file_row and read its bytes with read_spool_entry for the data_directory open_store opened, that key and the record's content_digest and size_bytes; the caller names a record, never a path, and this function does not check whether the run still holds its spool.
judgement.why: read_value_bytes must read both artifact areas but is not a publishing function, so obeying its required reads violates the exclusivity clause.

topics.topic: Whether remove_run_spool may modify the run spool despite the exclusivity claim
questions: Must remove_run_spool remain allowed to modify the run spool, or must the exclusive-access claim be narrowed to exclude cleanup functions?
Must remove_run_spool remain allowed to modify the run spool, or must the record_change note narrow its exclusivity claim so removal is also permitted?
Must the exclusivity claim permit remove_run_spool to modify the run spool, or must remove_run_spool cease removing it?

quotes: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST NOT publish, rewrite or re-check value bytes or a spooled file: a StoredValue carries no bytes, and record_change writes only records, so the content-addressed area and the run spool are read and written only by the functions that publish them.

remove_run_spool: [BEHAVIOR] MUST remove the spool of run_id with remove_spool_group for the data_directory open_store opened and run_id, which returns normally when that spool is absent; it writes no record.
judgement.why: remove_run_spool must modify spool storage although it is a cleanup function rather than a function that publishes the spool.

topics.topic: Whether artifact-access exclusivity permits required startup cleanup, replacement, and spool-removal operations
questions: Must the exclusivity claim be narrowed so start-up cleanup, replacement and spool removal may modify artifact storage, or must those required cleanup operations be removed?

quotes: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST NOT publish, rewrite or re-check value bytes or a spooled file: a StoredValue carries no bytes, and record_change writes only records, so the content-addressed area and the run spool are read and written only by the functions that publish them.

open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on data_directory itself, opened as a directory without following links and held for the life of the process, so the lock creates no file; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the temporary files an interrupted publish left in the content-addressed area and every file of that area whose digest no StoredValue names — a trial case's file fixture is itself a StoredValue of file carriage (M21), so no other record names a value file —, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area when absent; last, call remove_spool_temporaries for data_directory, which creates the spool area when absent and removes the temporaries of an interrupted spool publish, re-raising its SpoolInternalError as StoreInternalError.

spool_file: [BEHAVIOR] When no SpooledFile record names file's position, MUST publish content with publish_spool_entry for the data_directory open_store opened and file, which replaces a file no record names left at that position by a change that failed. The attempt_number of file is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file assigns none.

remove_run_spool: [BEHAVIOR] MUST remove the spool of run_id with remove_spool_group for the data_directory open_store opened and run_id, which returns normally when that spool is absent; it writes no record.
judgement.why: Although replacement by spool_file is publication, the same exclusivity clause is incompatible with the separately required startup cleanup and spool-removal operations.

topics.topic: Whether the prohibition must be classified as FORBIDDEN_ACTION separately from artifact-access policy
questions: The prohibition must be classified as [FORBIDDEN_ACTION], with any distinct artifact-access policy stated separately if needed.

quotes: record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST NOT publish, rewrite or re-check value bytes or a spooled file: a StoredValue carries no bytes, and record_change writes only records, so the content-addressed area and the run spool are read and written only by the functions that publish them.
judgement.why: The note's primary operative requirement is a prohibition of actions, but it is classified as artifact policy instead of the closed-registry class for prohibitions.
judgement.rule: - `[FORBIDDEN_ACTION]` — запрет действия: MUST NOT, never, no file I/O, no direct access.

topics.topic: Whether the spooled-file precondition must use positive normative modality
questions: The spooled-file precondition must use positive normative modality, for example “spooled files MUST already be published,” rather than lowercase “must”.

quotes: record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.
judgement.why: This lowercase-modality passage is unchanged from the closed version, and the added artifact-access note neither touched it nor made its modality matter.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
